item.title: SCP-5655: Perfect proof of "not all SCPs have to be grimdark"
item.content:encoded: Thank $DEITY for a break from killer side effects, world-ending threats, and monthly D-class terminations! Even the Foundation deserves to find an anomaly that's good clean fun (but not -J material) sometimes; the experiment logs were outstandingly well done, especially the "balanced budget" and "better key to happiness" wishes. Upvoted, wish I could legally upvote this skip more…

item.title: Out of Frame: +1
item.content:encoded:
This is a very interesting tale surrounding the Glittering Horizons Series. Admittedly, I really lack the context surrounding the series of events with Van Turner, the Department of Photography, and everything else. Regardless, this was an extremely fun little piece. I personally enjoyed the duality between Van Turner's proposal towards the Council and Joseph being chased down by his mysterious gunman. The action between the two was definitely there and really kept me engaged throughout. The progression between the two also really flowed well for me, and the ending definitely left me wondering. Why did they do this? What's the bigger play at hand here? What's the real reason behind this all? A wonderful piece narratively, with smooth prose and detailed imagery to really nail things together. Great job author!

Porting my feedback from the Art Exchange thread. My opinion remains unchanged. Great job!

item.title: SCP-5181:
item.content:encoded:
Disclaimer: I am not staff, I understand removal of this post or disciplinary actions taken against me for this. I informed #site17 but did not get a response before making this post.

Dear Vito loureiro,

This wiki is the English branch of the SCP community. I believe your article is written in Portugese.
The Portugese branch is most likely the place you are looking for.
You can also translate your article in English, as I believe some articles from other branches got included here.

I advise you to go to the chat so you can contact staff (from the English branch) to find the right course of action/options and answer any questions you may have.

item.title: SCP-5655:
item.content:encoded:
Upvoted, but there's one grammar thing:

Result: An used copy of Kerplunk

Since 'used' has a 'you' sound, it should be "a used copy'; if it was 'unused', which has an 'uh' sound, it would be 'An'. English is a dumb language.

item.title: SCP-4144:
item.content:encoded:
This was deeply disturbing and I hated it.
...as it turns out, only the first part of that statement was true (for me)

My thought process while reading this went from 'what?' to 'what.' to 'what the fuck.' in record time. Brilliant execution, concept, tone, and content, while also skilfully incorporating humour without breaking immersion. +1.
Bonus points for making me briefly consider not eating breakfast not out of time constraints, nor for lack of hunger, but out of fear.

item.title: SCP-5655:
item.content:encoded:
I would have tested if he can pick locks, know safe combinaisons, know which SCP containment procedures need improvement from a list of apparently very low danger SCPs who cost much effort to contain, and ask him to suggest some wishes that would please me without mindcontrol.

Failing that, he can always be used to reset the mousetraps around the cafeteria —- the cook is always looking to cut corners into the meat budget.
